+ Their position.

I did some testing today on an AST2600 EVB and this function is consistently taking > 500ms, which makes the SSIF driver abort the command.  I captured these timestamps with busctl:

```
6.691       start
6.696 :+005 get bootstrapping enabled
6.697 :+001 return
6.700 :+003 mapper subtree paths
6.704 :+004 return
6.706 :+002 get managed objects
6.707 :+001 return
6.727 :+020 create user
6.819 :+092 return
6.951 :+132 get role id
6.953 :+002 return
6.956 :+003 set user priv
7.056 :+100 return
7.142 :+086 set bootstrap account
7.150 :+008 return
7.191 :+041 set user enabled
7.228 :+037 return
7.269 :+041 end
```

There is a 132ms gap between creating the user and getting the role id, which seems to be where we generate the password.

Also setting the user attributes takes a bit:
100 + 8 + 37 = 145ms
Can I asked why the SSIF driver abort the command when it take more than 500ms?

There is this comment in the driver:

```
/*
 * IPMI 2.0 Spec, section 12.7 SSIF Timing,
 * Request-to-Response Time is T6max(250ms) - T1max(20ms) - 3ms = 227ms
 * Recover ssif_bmc from busy state if it takes up to 500ms
 */
#define RESPONSE_TIMEOUT                        500 /* ms */
```

Can you check if bypass the creating password steps (hard code the password) helps improve the time out?
I implemented code following the Redfish host interface spec, the spec does not mention which interface can use this interface and how to deal with the time out in creating the user name and passwords.
There is no guarantee that all the message in SSIF interface can finish in 500ms. What happens when BMC is busy and can't response the message in 500ms? What happens in BMCLess?

If you have any idea in improving the creating passwords and user time, feel free to propose but as my opinion we should not compromise the security just because the SSIF has 500ms time out.

> Can you check if bypass

That was the first thing I tried and it doesn't make any difference.

> There is no guarantee that all the message in SSIF interface can finish in 500ms.

I agree.  I suppose if the command could be processed with the bmc under no/light load, we could respond with a busy response when under heavy load so the host retries.  but we can't even respond in time with no load, so that doesn't really help.

> What happens in BMCLess?

I don't understand.  If there is no bmc, the host side ssif driver isn't even going to load so we won't be doing ssif.

> If you have any idea in improving the creating passwords and user time

The only thing I could come up with is some kind of super-optimized user mgr interface.  We are making a lot of dbus calls back and forth to the user manager - I suspect we could shave off a fair amount of time there.  But that seems like a bigger problem with the user manager.

So Quan@Ampere wrote the bmc ssif driver and the 500ms timeout.  Do they still work at Ampere?  Maybe you could chat with them about it.   I patched my kernel to 1s and the command work fine.

@vernon.mauery@gmail.com I'd be curious to get your take on this if you have time, thanks.

I think that the 500ms timeout seems very short. Depending on what else the BMC is doing at the time, it might not take much to have any IPMI command timeout, much less one that is involved, like creating a user.

I am also not opposed to optimizing the user management interface. It seems like we should be able to just provide all the details we want for the user in one go. I am not sure what the bottlenecks are in actually creating the user, but a second is a long time to wait and that should be addressed.

Thanks @vernon.mauery@gmail.com.  The 500ms is 2x a number from the IPMI spec itself in the SSIF section, so I wasn't sure if increasing that timeout was reasonable or if IPMI implementations have just gotten slower over the years and the spec is out of touch.

I'm thinking about response for the Ipmi request right after handler has the username and password. The process creating the user account us IPMI API will be handled in a timer which will be started before handler response for the request.

The Cont of this approach is if creating the account is failed. The host application, service will not know, and it will failed to access redfish host interface although it got the BootStrap account from the mmc service.

About the delay in access D-Bus to check the existing of the default `bootstrap0`, I think we can use internal variable which will be inited in the start of ipmid service. BMC also need handle adding/removing the user object path to detect the remove of bootstrap0.
